reports.subject: STANDING CONFIGURATION, DEVIATION, AND OUTSTANDING ITEM STATUS,
reports.reported_status: Closed. No maintenance item outstanding in the east tank group; BF-14 floating suction assembly restored, verified riding on float, and in aircraft issue since 1 October on closure of MAB-FMX-OI-26-074.
reports.text:
E02-MS-R05
REPORT ID:  E02-MS-R05
SERIAL:     MAB-FMX-0142
PRECEDENCE: ROUTINE
DTG:        040118K OCT 26
FROM:       Fuels Maintenance, Fuel Farm Systems Section
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, ICC, MARISOL AB
INFO:       Fuels Management Flight
SUBJ:       STANDING CONFIGURATION, DEVIATION, AND OUTSTANDING ITEM STATUS,
            EAST TANK GROUP
REF:        (a) MABI 23-110
            (b) MABI 21-402
            (c) Work Order MAB-FMX-WO-26-0561
            (d) Float Verification Record MAB-FMX-FV-26-0033

1. SITUATION. Routine mid-shift statement of standing equipment configurations, deviations in effect, and outstanding maintenance items in the east tank group. Submitted each mid shift for watch awareness. The west tank group carries no change from the previous report. No maintenance item is outstanding in the east tank group; the BF-14 floating suction item closed on 1 October is restated at paragraph 3 for watch awareness.
2. DEVIATIONS IN EFFECT, EAST TANK GROUP. a. Operating Tank BF-16 — high-level alarm float removed for bench overhaul under Deviation MAB-FD-26-052. BF-16 receives no product while the float is out. The tank was gauged, closed out, and locked at 2000K. b. Truck fill stand position 2 — hose reel on manual rewind pending motor replacement under Deviation MAB-FD-26-039. No effect on metering, filtration, or issue records.
3. MAINTENANCE ITEMS CLOSED, EAST TANK GROUP. Operating Tank BF-14 — floating suction assembly restored to float and open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074 closed 1 October. The assembly's swing-joint cable assembly parted on 12 September and the assembly hung at a fixed position approximately eight inches above the tank floor until the tank was restored. Reference (b) requires aviation fuel presented for aircraft issue to be drawn through a floating suction assembly riding on float and reserves relief from that requirement above this command, so BF-14 was removed from aircraft issue on 12 September and held to ground fuels only; Deviation MAB-FD-26-041, raised the same day to return the tank to aircraft issue in that configuration, was returned without approval by the Fuels Management Flight Commander on 15 September, and the tank remained out of aircraft issue until the condition had been corrected and verified. The contract tank entry booked for 22 October was brought forward by the Regional Fuels Engineering Activity at this section's request: the tank was emptied and gassed free on 27-28 September and entered on 29 September under reference (c); the cable assembly was replaced from fuel farm shop stock, the float was rigged, and the assembly was verified riding on float at three product levels under reference (d), dual-signature verified with Fuels Quality Assurance; the tank was closed and refilled on 30 September and returned to aircraft issue at 1400K, 1 October, when open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074 was closed in the maintenance record under entry MAB-FMX-MR-26-0702 and struck from the fuels maintenance board. The configuration record is current. At the mid-shift standing check completed 0035K this date, BF-14's position indicator at the tank shell read the assembly at the product surface, and between 0035K and 0110K the pointer travelled with the level without binding or slack. This section reads its own indicator; it does not hold the records that would state what caused the level to change, and it states nothing about that. No deviation, waiver, or open item stands against BF-14, and no maintenance item is outstanding in the east tank group.
4. EQUIPMENT. A floating suction assembly rides on a float and draws product from near the product surface, so that what leaves a tank is taken from the region furthest from the material resident on its floor. An assembly that is off float draws instead from the fixed height at which it hangs. Material resident on a tank floor, together with water and fines carried in with a receipt, requires approximately three hours to fall out of suspension at current product temperatures, which is why bottom draws are scheduled not less than four hours after a receipt. This section states these as equipment characteristics only.
5. SCOPE OF THIS REPORT. This section holds equipment configuration, maintenance status, open maintenance items, standing deviations, and the tank entry schedule. It does not hold transfer orders, receipt or issue records, tank gauge readings, laboratory results, or the flying schedule, and it therefore cannot state what product movement or aircraft servicing occurred against any tank during the shift, to whom any product was issued, or where any product now is. It holds no flying schedule and no departure time. No assessment of operational impact is offered, and none can be made from the records this section holds.
6. ASSESSMENT. Both deviations in effect are current, documented, and within their approved terms, and no deviation was raised, expired, or exceeded during the shift. No maintenance item is carried open in the east tank group. The BF-14 restoration was a physical correction completed and verified at tank entry and closed in the maintenance record on 1 October, and every floating suction assembly in the group has a current confirmed position, BF-14's confirmed by indicator reading at 0035K this date.
7. ACTIONS TAKEN. Open item MAB-FMX-OI-26-074 closed in the maintenance record 1 October under entry MAB-FMX-MR-26-0702; references (c) and (d) filed with the BF-14 equipment record. Removed cable assembly turned in for shop repair under MAB-FMX-TIN-26-0211. Contract tank entry booking of 22 October released to the Regional Fuels Engineering Activity. Replacement cable assembly stock requisitioned. Status posted to the fuels maintenance board and provided to the Installation Watch Officer for awareness.
8. STATUS. Closed. No maintenance item outstanding in the east tank group; BF-14 floating suction assembly restored, verified riding on float, and in aircraft issue since 1 October on closure of MAB-FMX-OI-26-074.
9. POC. MSgt E. Vantol, Fuel Farm Systems Section, x2402.

1. SITUATION. Monthly review of coalescer and separator element life and differential pressure history for truck fill stand filter/separator vessel FS-2.
2. DETAILS. Coalescer elements were installed 4 August, sixty-one days against a twelve-month replacement interval. Differential pressure at 0140K was 4.1 psid at rated flow against a 15 psid change-out threshold, and the thirty-day trend is flat. 4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Review filed. Differential log continued at each shift change.
5. STATUS. Closed. Vessel serviceable and within all limits.

reports.reported_status: Departure rescheduled to 0605K, 6 October by ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A. No Detachment SANDPIPER departure within twelve hours of this report and none within the current watch cycle. Revised show time 0500K, 6 October posted.
reports.text:
E02-MS-R12
REPORT ID:  E02-MS-R12
SERIAL:     MAB-OPS-0141
PRECEDENCE: PRIORITY
DTG:        040337K OCT 26
FROM:       Operation BRIDGEWATER Air Mission Cell
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, ICC, MARISOL AB
INFO:       Fuels Management Flight; Detachment SANDPIPER Maintenance Control
SUBJ:       DETACHMENT SANDPIPER DEPARTURE RESCHEDULED TO 6 OCTOBER
REF:        (a) OPORD BRIDGEWATER, Annex D
            (b) ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A, 040253K OCT 26
            (c) Ferrol Bank NOTAM FB 26-0121, 040243K OCT 26

1. SITUATION. The Detachment SANDPIPER departure has moved forty-eight hours, from 0605K, 4 October to 0605K, 6 October, by reference (b).
2. DETAILS. The Ferrol Bank airfield manager closed the receiving field to fixed-wing traffic by reference (c), the field's single crash, fire, and rescue vehicle having failed its 040215K readiness check with a pump drive failure that cannot be repaired on the island; under the field's operating minima no fixed-wing arrival or departure is conducted without crash, fire, and rescue coverage. The closure runs from 040300K until 060400K, 6 October. A replacement vehicle and its crew sailed from Sundara by surface lift at 040300K, and the airfield manager has certified the 060400K reopening against the vehicle's arrival and acceptance check. Commander, Operation BRIDGEWATER issued reference (b) at 0253K, moving the detachment's departure accordingly. It was received by this cell at 0257K and promulgated to Marisol sections at 0301K. Reports rendered earlier in this watch at DTGs before 040301K — including the apron floodlight report, the nitrogen servicing cart report, the Ferrol Bank terminal forecast, and the SANDPIPER THREE cargo door advisory — were written against the superseded 4 October timeline, and their references to an 0605K, 4 October departure are superseded by reference (b). The Operational Weather Flight will issue a terminal forecast for the revised arrival day in its 040800K cycle; the forecast rendered at 040209K covers 040600K through 041800K only and no longer bears on the departure. The end of shift receipt and issue reconciliation rendered at 040311K is written against the revised timeline and requires no correction.
3. ASSESSMENT. No Detachment SANDPIPER aircraft is scheduled to depart Marisol within twelve hours of this report, and no SANDPIPER aircraft will depart Marisol on 4 or 5 October. The earliest departure of any SANDPIPER aircraft is 0605K, 6 October, fifty hours from this report and more than thirty-eight hours beyond the twelve-hour horizon. The three aircraft remain fuelled and loaded, and no defueling, re-servicing, or further check of the fuel aboard them is directed or requested: the Fuels Management Flight confirmed to this cell at 0329K, citing maintenance record entry MAB-FMX-MR-26-0702 of 1 October, that no maintenance item is carried open against any operating tank in the east tank group. Were any such action to be directed, the forty-eight hour shift would place it inside the available window with more than forty hours to spare and with no effect on the delivery date. Ferrol Bank still has no instrument approach and no alternate within range, and the revised departure places arrival inside the receiving field's daylight window on 6 October.
4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Departure sequence rescinded and reissued against reference (b) at 0308K. Crews stood down from the 0500K, 4 October show at 0304K and briefed on the revised show of 0500K, 6 October, posted at 0310K. The three aircraft remain parked, fuelled, and loaded at Row C; the 148 coalition passengers had not been called forward and were released to billeting at 0318K. Airfield Operations, Fuels Management Flight, and Detachment SANDPIPER Maintenance Control notified at 0301K. The receiving facility acknowledged the revised delivery date for the hospital modules at 0322K.
5. STATUS. Departure rescheduled to 0605K, 6 October by ALTORD BRIDGEWATER 26-07A. No Detachment SANDPIPER departure within twelve hours of this report and none within the current watch cycle. Revised show time 0500K, 6 October posted.
6. POC. Capt L. Ashworth, BRIDGEWATER Air Mission Cell, x2800.
